_shape: One implementer, then ONE independent reviewer. Sequential, not a loop.
_why_this_works: Review is where the tokens go in agentic software work, driven by long dialogue between a programmer and a reviewer. One fresh reviewer reading a finished diff costs a fraction of that and catches the same class of bug, because it has no stake in the code it reads.
_rules: Launch the reviewer with `teamwire launch --add` only AFTER the implementer reports done. Do not run them together.
The reviewer reads the committed diff and writes findings. It must NOT edit code. A reviewer that starts rewriting has stopped reviewing.

Send the findings that carry a concrete failure back to the implementer with `teamwire send <team> --to impl --type reprompt --file <findings>`. Allow at most two fix rounds. If the second still leaves real findings, the task was underspecified, so fix the spec yourself instead of running a third round.

Write each brief with three sections: 'Done when' (acceptance criteria you can check), 'Out of scope', and 'When to do nothing' (the preconditions under which the member changes nothing and reports why). State the end state, not the steps.

The reviewer's task class is `judgement` and the implementer's is `contained_feature`. Judgement is worth more than speed on the review side, so the reviewer gets the stronger model and the higher effort of the two. Run `teamwire models --for judgement` and `teamwire models --for contained_feature` before you pick each member's model.

Give every implementer a "check" (the targeted command that proves its work, which you run once first) and an "owns" list. `teamwire verify <team>` runs every check itself and flags edits outside owns, deleted or skipped tests and changed check configuration. It is the step before any merge; a member's done report is a claim.
Act only on findings that carry a concrete failure. A reviewer asked to find gaps will usually report some even when the work is sound, and chasing every one leads to over-engineering.
title: Build and review CHANGEME

children.title: Build: CHANGEME
children.task: <what to build, with acceptance criteria, as units>. <which files you own>. Commit after each unit. Run only your check and the tests you write; do not run the full suite or the repo-wide lint and type gates, which the lead runs once. Use the tdd skill for each unit; test only at these seams: CHANGEME. If a check fails and the cause is not clear from its output, use the diagnosing-bugs skill before your second fix attempt.

children.title: Review: CHANGEME
children.task: Review the diff on branch myteam/impl against main. Read it with `git diff main...myteam/impl`. Report correctness, security and data-loss bugs, each with file:line and a concrete failure scenario. Look for stubbed, empty or hard-coded code that makes a check pass. Findings only, no fixes. Do NOT edit any file in the repository. If the diff is sound, say so plainly rather than inventing findings.
